title: Fynaptix · Space Economy Research
heading: Space Economy Intelligence
subheading: Launch, satellites, constellations & the post-SpaceX-IPO landscape
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Space is capital-intensive with heavy government-customer concentration. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Global space economy estimated at ~$626B in 2026; Goldman Sachs and McKinsey both project a climb to $1.8T by 2035 alongside a rising wave of sector M&A

kpis.sub: BELOW POST-IPO HIGH · STARSHIP FLIGHT 14 NOW SLATED SEPT 18
kpis.label: SPCX closed at $151.21 on Sept 13 — up from $147.95 a week earlier and well above the $135 IPO price, but still ~33% below its $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14 (first orbital attempt, first Ship tower-catch, ~20-satellite Starlink V3 delivery) has slipped from a Sept 15 target to Sept 18 (backup Sept 19), after Booster 21 completed a full 33-engine static fire on Aug 28

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD STARTUP FUNDING · U.S. CAPTURES ~63% OF GLOBAL TOTAL
kpis.label: Crunchbase-tracked global private investment in space/satellite startups holds at a record $20.3B for 2026, already the highest annual tally on record with four months still to go; U.S. companies captured roughly $12.7B (~63%) of that total, and Stoke Space alone closed a $1B tranche of it on Sept 8

kpis.sub: NEUTRON'S LIKELY DEBUT YEAR · ARK BUYS $45M OF RKLB
kpis.label: Rocket Lab shares (~$62, market cap ~$40B) remain well off their highs even after a record Q2, but Cathie Wood's ARK bought $45M of RKLB stock this week and Raymond James initiated coverage at Outperform with an $80 target; the company completed its 16th Electron launch of 2026 (95th overall) on Sept 11, while Neutron's maiden flight still looks pointed at 2027 and the Iridium deal remains targeted for a mid-2027 close

tiers.label: Scale Players
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Q2 revenue $7.8B (+92% YoY), with Starlink/connectivity revenue up 66% YoY to $4.3B (~$17B annualized) and 12M subscribers, adding 500k+ new subs a month; connectivity remains the only profitable segment ($1.66B operating profit). Shares closed at $151.21 on Sept 13, up from $147.95 a week earlier and well above the $135 IPO price, though still ~33% below the $225.64 post-IPO high
rows.watch for: Starship Flight 14 — first orbital attempt, first tower-catch of Ship, ~20-satellite Starlink V3 delivery — has slipped from a Sept 15 target to Sept 18 (backup Sept 19), after Booster 21 completed a full 33-engine static fire on Aug 28 and Ship 41 finished its own six-engine test the week before; four more share-unlock tranches through Dec 8, 2026; Starlink ARPU down 22% YoY as international/lower-priced plans scale

rows.angle: Launched its 16th Electron mission of 2026 (95th overall) on Sept 11 from New Zealand, and Cathie Wood's ARK bought $45M of RKLB stock this week; Raymond James initiated coverage at Outperform with an $80 target and unveiled a new IMM Apex germanium-free solar cell aimed at easing space-power cost pressure. Record Q2 revenue of $234M (+62% YoY) and a record $2.36B backlog still stand, with Q3 guided to $250-265M
rows.watch for: Despite the institutional buying and new coverage, shares (~$62, market cap ~$40B) remain roughly 58%+ off their highs for the year and below the $67.50 floor of the Iridium exchange-ratio collar; Neutron's maiden flight still looks more likely to slip into 2027 after January's tank-pressure-test rupture, and the Iridium close remains targeted for mid-2027

rows.angle: CEO Sam Mehta and CFO Ken Sharp laid out a three-pillar strategy (multi-domain sensing, spectrum dominance, missiles) at the Sept 9 Jefferies Global Industrials Conference, and L3Harris landed a new $4.7B undefinitized contract from Lockheed Martin for PAC-3 MSE interceptor propulsion systems over seven years, expanding Camden, Arkansas production. Still building 18 of the SDA's Tranche 3 tracking satellites under the $1.75B AMDT3 award (with Sierra Space)
rows.watch for: Shares are now testing 52-week lows near $250-253, down more than 30% over six months, as the securities-claims investigation tied to Kubasik's August ouster remains open; also sits in the Defense sleeve — don't double-count exposure

tiers.label: Growth / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: BlueBirds 12 and 13 are fully deployed, a new gateway opened in New Zealand, and integration testing continues with Vodafone, Orange, Telefónica and Deutsche Telekom; Berenberg holds a $92 price target. Q2 revenue rose to $31.5M on a reaffirmed $150-200M FY26 guide, with $3.7B+ of cash and a $1.3B backlog
rows.watch for: Q2's loss came in wider than expected at $0.77/share, and the broader 14-analyst base rates the stock a Hold with a median target of $83 (range $43-108); shares holding near ~$62, with the $1B convertible-note dilution overhang and BlueBirds 14-16 shipping timeline still the swing factors

rows.angle: Booked a new IM 300 platform order (two units) from an undisclosed customer out of its high-volume Palo Alto facility, extending diversification beyond lunar landers alongside the $600M+ GEO satellite contract, the JPL-selected EAGLE-VSWIR mission, the Tranche 3 missile-defense build with L3Harris, and the Goonhilly/COMSAT acquisitions
rows.watch for: Director Kamal Ghaffarian sold roughly $1.48M of stock on Sept 8-9, right after the IM 300 order was announced, and shares kept sliding to ~$14.62 — 69% below the 52-week high of $46.75 though still up 76% over the past year; Goonhilly/COMSAT integration and IM-3 Nova-C lander progress remain the operational watch items

rows.angle: Q2 revenue of $116.1M (+58% YoY) delivered Planet's first profitable quarter as a public company, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.02 beating estimates
rows.watch for: The ~$103M next-quarter guide came in about 10.5% below estimates, triggering three analyst price-target cuts this week — Northland to $40 (from $50), Craig-Hallum to $35 (from $49), Deutsche Bank to $28 (from $36) — and shares fell to ~$16.46, testing the rising 320-day moving average and well off the $51.76 May high

rows.angle: Record Q2 revenue of $117.1M (+89.6% YoY), record 27.8% gross margin, and a record $542.1M backlog (book-to-bill 1.42); reaffirmed FY26 guidance of $450-500M with 90% visibility, and showcased its Penguin UAS and Octopus payloads at the Sept 10-11 Rīga Conference as the largest UAS supplier in the Baltics
rows.watch for: Shares held a steady $10.77-$11.21 band this week with no fresh negative news; BofA's Aug 31 $8 target still sits below the quote, but sustaining margin gains as revenue scales — and now as the Baltics defense-tech push adds a new growth vector — remains the key watch item

private_watchlist.name: Blue Origin
private_watchlist.note: Root-cause work on the May 28 New Glenn pad explosion continues, with Blue Origin skipping a full transporter-erector rebuild in favor of a simpler wheeled-vehicle-plus-crane approach so it can still target a return to flight before year-end; SpaceX veterans have told press they're skeptical New Glenn flies from the rebuilt pad in 2026 given the scope of the infrastructure work.

private_watchlist.name: Firefly Aerospace
private_watchlist.note: Signed a new multi-launch agreement with SSC Space on Sept 9 for two Alpha launches from Sweden's Esrange Space Center (targeted no earlier than 2028), and Morgan Stanley initiated coverage Sept 2 at Equal Weight with a $52 target; shares trade around $23, with a SpaceX rideshare crunch seen as a tailwind for Firefly's and Rocket Lab's dedicated small-launch businesses. Record Q2 revenue of $117.7M (+659% YoY) on a $1.5B backlog (95% of FY26 guidance already booked).

private_watchlist.name: Stoke Space
private_watchlist.note: Closed its Series E at $1B on Sept 8, co-led by Point72 Ventures and Spark Capital, bringing total capital raised to $2.3B; publicly unveiled the Nova Pathfinder vehicle, but the first orbital flight has slipped from 'end of 2026' to 'early 2027.' Nova Block 2 (15 metric tons to LEO) is now targeted for 2029.

bear_case.title: Capital intensity
bear_case.description: Rockets and constellations burn billions before returns — Stoke Space's Series E closed at $1B on Sept 8 (total raised now $2.3B) to fund Nova Pathfinder, whose first flight has already slipped from 'end of 2026' to 'early 2027'; dilution and debt stay chronic among small caps (RKLB's Iridium bridge facility, ASTS's $1B convertible notes).

bear_case.title: Government concentration
bear_case.description: Much of the sector's revenue is NASA/DoD — L3Harris just landed a new $4.7B Lockheed contract for PAC-3 MSE interceptor propulsion on top of its $1.75B AMDT3 Golden Dome award, yet LHX shares are testing 52-week lows anyway, a reminder that a growing government backlog doesn't guarantee a re-rating while a securities-claims investigation sits unresolved.

bear_case.title: SpaceX absorbs the value / sector repricing
bear_case.description: A dominant incumbent with launch-cost leverage can compress everyone else's margins — SPCX has climbed back to $151.21 but remains ~33% below its post-IPO high, and even its own near-term catalyst has slipped: Starship Flight 14 moved from a Sept 15 target to Sept 18/19. Meanwhile RKLB's record Q2 didn't stop shares from sitting 58%+ off their highs, a widening gap between operating results and price across the sector.

bear_case.title: Binary mission risk
bear_case.description: One failed test or slipped date can move a small-cap sharply: Stoke's Nova Pathfinder just slipped from year-end 2026 to early 2027, Neutron still looks pointed at 2027 after January's tank-pressure-test rupture, and Blue Origin's New Glenn return-to-flight target faces open skepticism from SpaceX veterans over the pad-rebuild timeline. SpaceX's own prospectus flags "key man" dependence on Elon Musk.

catalysts.title: Rocket Lab launches 16th Electron of 2026; ARK buys in
catalysts.description: Rocket Lab completed its 95th Electron launch overall and 16th of the year from New Zealand, while Cathie Wood's ARK disclosed a $45M purchase of RKLB stock and Raymond James initiated coverage at Outperform with an $80 target.

catalysts.title: L3Harris lands $4.7B Lockheed interceptor contract
catalysts.description: L3Harris received an undefinitized seven-year, $4.7B contract from Lockheed Martin to produce propulsion systems for the PAC-3 MSE interceptor, as CEO Sam Mehta outlined a missiles/space/comms strategy at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference.

catalysts.title: Firefly signs Sweden launch deal; Stoke unveils Nova Pathfinder
catalysts.description: Firefly Aerospace agreed to a two-launch deal with SSC Space for Alpha flights from Esrange, Sweden, the same week Stoke Space publicly unveiled its Nova Pathfinder vehicle and confirmed its $1B Series E.

catalysts.title: Stoke Space closes $1B Series E; Nova slips to early 2027
catalysts.description: The round, co-led by Point72 Ventures and Spark Capital, brings Stoke's total raised to $2.3B, but Nova Pathfinder's first orbital flight has moved from 'end of 2026' to 'early 2027.'

catalysts.title: Planet Labs beats on revenue, but light guide triggers target cuts
catalysts.description: Planet's Q2 revenue of $116.1M topped estimates and delivered its first profitable quarter, but a soft ~$103M next-quarter guide drove three analyst price-target cuts and pushed shares down to ~$16.46.

catalysts.title: Starship Flight 14 date shifts to Sept 18
catalysts.description: An FCC filing and static-fire completions (Booster 21's full 33-engine test on Aug 28) point to Sept 18 (backup Sept 19) for Starship's first true orbital attempt, carrying ~20 Starlink V3 satellites.

etfs.name: Procure Space
etfs.summary: Pure-play, revenue-weighted (RKLB, PL, VSAT, MDA, ASTS top holdings); roughly +55-58% YTD per recent readings — RKLB's continued weakness and PL's post-earnings slide are partial drags, though RDW's steadiness and ASTS's stability help offset them

etfs.name: ARK Space Exploration
etfs.summary: Actively managed, broader tech adjacency; roughly +25-28% YTD, +70-76% 1yr — still lagging the pure-play index funds

etfs.name: SPDR Kensho Final Frontiers
etfs.summary: Equal-weight, space + defense + deep-sea blend; roughly +55-58% YTD — L3Harris's slide toward 52-week lows is a new drag on the defense side of the blend

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: Rocket Lab
positions.note: Cathie Wood's ARK bought $45M of RKLB shares this week and Raymond James initiated coverage at Outperform with an $80 target, but shares (~$62, still 58%+ off highs) haven't followed yet — Neutron remains pointed at 2027 and the mid-2027 Iridium close is unchanged; holding weight roughly flat as institutional validation offsets continued price weakness.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: Shares are now testing 52-week lows near $250-253, down over 30% in six months, even after landing a new $4.7B Lockheed contract for PAC-3 MSE interceptor propulsion; the still-open securities-claims investigation from the Kubasik ouster is weighing more than the backlog growth, so trimming weight. Also sits in your Defense sleeve — don't double-count the exposure.

positions.name: Redwire
positions.note: No negative news this week — Redwire showcased its Penguin UAS and Octopus payloads at the Rīga Conference (Sept 10-11), reinforcing defense-tech diversification beyond its $542M core backlog, while shares held a steady $10.77-$11.21 band; raising weight further as the sector's most consistent execution story.

positions.name: AST SpaceMobile
positions.note: BlueBird 12 and 13 are fully deployed and Berenberg holds a $92 target, but Q2's loss came in wider than expected at $0.77/share and the broader analyst base rates it a Hold (median target $83, range $43-108); holding weight flat as deployment progress and earnings quality pull in opposite directions.

positions.name: Intuitive Machines
positions.note: The new IM 300 platform order is genuine diversification, but director Kamal Ghaffarian sold $1.48M of stock in the two days right after the announcement, and shares kept sliding to $14.62 (69% below the 52-week high); holding at the small speculative size that binary mission risk and this insider selling both argue for.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Shares closed at $151.21 on Sept 13, still ~33% below the $225.64 post-IPO high; Starship Flight 14 — the next real proof point — has slipped from a Sept 15 target to Sept 18/19, after Booster 21's full 33-engine static fire on Aug 28. UK investors wanting SpaceX exposure without chasing the US listing can get indirect access via Scottish Mortgage (SMT, covered on the Baillie Gifford page).

positions.name: Planet Labs
positions.note: Q2 revenue beat and delivered a first profitable quarter, but the light ~$103M next-quarter guide triggered three analyst price-target cuts this week (Northland to $40, Craig-Hallum to $35, Deutsche Bank to $28), and shares kept sliding to ~$16.46 — growth deceleration keeps this off Core.

positions.name: Iridium Communications
positions.note: Deal economics remain the whole story: RKLB shares stay well off their highs and Neutron's own timeline is still pointed at 2027, adding execution risk on top of the still-distant mid-2027 close; RKLB stock remains the cleaner way to express the same view.
